discovery: Horizon-scale imaging of black holes with the Event Horizon Telescope

nominees.name: Sheperd S. Doeleman
nominees.affiliation: Center for Astrophysics | Harvard & Smithsonian, USA

nominees.name: James M. Moran
nominees.affiliation: Center for Astrophysics | Harvard & Smithsonian, USA

subfield: Astrophysics / Very-long-baseline interferometry and black hole physics
motivation: Stellar orbits established that a compact object of four million solar masses sits at the Galactic Centre. Proving that it is a black hole, with a horizon-scale shadow, required a different technology. Falcke and collaborators predicted in 2000 that the shadow of Sgr A* should be visible with millimetre VLBI. Moran pioneered the interferometric techniques and the submillimetre infrastructure that made such an array possible. Doeleman led the decades-long effort to link telescopes across the planet into an Earth-sized instrument, the Event Horizon Telescope, which in 2019 imaged the ring around M87* and in 2022 imaged Sgr A*. Repeated campaigns, including the 2024 polarized image of Sgr A* and multi-year M87* data, confirmed ring sizes consistent with general relativity. Their work turned a long-standing theoretical object into a directly imaged one and opened horizon-scale tests of gravity.
